Marissa — quick technical readout / recommendation based on the attached traffic sample and target latencies: 

Short answers up front:
- Cold GPU spin-up: ~45–90s depending on instance type and image warm-up; safe planning value = 60s
- Warm pool: recommend a prewarmed pool sized to absorb ~2x baseline (so for baseline 50 concurrent, plan warm pool for ~100 concurrent sessions)
- Burst capacity: we can provide short burst capacity (3x warm pool) for up to ~120s using ephemeral warm-burst slots backed by excess cluster capacity; beyond that requests will queue or fallback to a lower-cost model variant
- Queueing behavior: FIFO queue with configurable max-wait (we recommend <=10s for UX); requests will be rejected after max-wait if capacity not available. Priority routing can be implemented (interactive > batch).

Details / reasoning:
- Streaming workloads favor small batch windows (10–30ms) to minimize initial token latency; that reduces batching efficiency so plan for higher baseline capacity than non-streaming workloads.
- KV cache warm-up: for repeated sessions the cache reaches useful hit rates after first few tokens; to optimize initial-token latency consider sticky routing to warm instances for returning users or use a small cache prefill on session start.
- Warm pool sizing: given 50 baseline concurrent and 400–500 peak, suggested configuration:
  * Prewarm: 100 concurrent capacity (absorbs baseline + 1x buffer)
  * Ephemeral burst slots: allow 2 additional burst multipliers (total burst capacity ~300 concurrent above warm pool) for up to 120s. This matches your 400–500 spikes.
  * Fallback policy: after burst window, degrade to lower-cost model variant (quantized) for noncritical sessions, or present queued wait UX for critical interactive flows.
- Scale-up knobs: autoscaler should attempt horizontal scale first (add agents to pool) and only fallback to spinning larger instances when needed. For GPU provisioning we estimate 60s median scale-up; to hit <250–350ms p95 initial-token during spikes rely on warm+burst above.

Operational notes:
- For contractual SLOs (p95): we recommend specifying two bands — baseline SLA (applies when warm pool + burst available) and degraded SLA (when exceeding burst threshold or during longer outages).
- Observability: expose token-level latency, queue depth, and warm-pool utilization to FastPay dashboards; we'll share a sample dashboard link after we sync.

Attachments: I attached a quick architecture_diagram.png and I've updated the SLO worksheet values inline (will send a revised worksheet if you want).

If that looks good I can convert these recommendations into a short configuration doc we can share with Amelia and infra@fastpay.com.
